        organization_id: orgId,

        payload: dto as unknown as Record<string, unknown>,

    );
    // ── f. Update contact with call analysis data ────────────────────────────
    if ((dto.event === 'call_ended' || dto.event === 'call_analyzed') && dto.call_analysis) {
      await this.updateContactFromCallAnalysis(orgId, contact.id, dto.call_analysis);
    }
    // ── g. Post-call: upsert one system message into the conversation timeline ─
    // call_ended and call_analyzed both fire for the same call, and the later
    // one is the first to carry the recording URL and summary. Keying on the
    // call alone (not the event) keeps a single card in the inbox and lets the
    // second event fill in what the first one did not have yet.
    if (dto.event === 'call_ended' || dto.event === 'call_analyzed') {
      await this.upsertCallMessage(orgId, conversation.id, call, dto);

    // ── h. Emit RabbitMQ events ──────────────────────────────────────────────
    if (dto.event === 'call_started') {
      this.rmqClient.emit(RABBITMQ_QUEUES.CALL_STARTED, {
        organization_id: orgId,
        conversation_id: conversation.id,
        contact_id: contact.id,
        call: { id: call.id, external_call_id: call.external_call_id },
      });
      void this.realtimeBroadcast?.notifyOrg(orgId, {
        id: call.id,
        type: 'voice',
        title: dto.direction === 'outbound' ? 'Llamada saliente' : 'Llamada entrante',
        description: dto.direction === 'outbound' ? `A ${phoneTo}` : `De ${phoneFrom}`,
        href: `/inbox?conversationId=${conversation.id}`,
        conversationId: conversation.id,
        contactId: contact.id,
      });
      void this.webhookDispatcher?.dispatch('voice.call.started', orgId, {
        call_id: call.id,
        phone_from: call.phone_from,
        phone_to: call.phone_to,
      });
    }
    if (dto.event === 'call_ended' || dto.event === 'call_analyzed') {
      this.rmqClient.emit(RABBITMQ_QUEUES.CALL_COMPLETED, {
        organization_id: orgId,
        conversation_id: conversation.id,
    conversationId: string,
    phoneFrom: string,
    phoneTo: string,
  ): Promise<CallEntity> {
    // Check Redis dedup cache first
    const cacheKey = `call:ext:${dto.call_id}`;
    const cachedId = await this.redis.get(cacheKey);
    let call: CallEntity | null = null;
    if (cachedId) {
      call = await this.callRepo.findOne({ where: { id: cachedId } });
    }
    if (!call) {
      call = await this.callRepo.findOne({ where: { external_call_id: dto.call_id } });
    }
    if (!call) {
      call = this.callRepo.create({
        organization_id: orgId,
        contact_id: contactId,
        conversation_id: conversationId,
        external_call_id: dto.call_id,
        phone_from: phoneFrom,
        phone_to: phoneTo,
        direction: dto.direction ?? 'inbound',
        status: 'initiated',
        provider: 'retell',
        channel: 'voice',
      });
    } else if (dto.direction && call.direction !== dto.direction) {
      // Backfill direction if an earlier event created the row without it.
      call.direction = dto.direction;
    }
    // Apply status transitions
    switch (dto.event) {
      case 'call_started':
        call.status = 'in_progress';
        call.started_at = new Date();
        break;
      case 'call_ended':
      case 'call_analyzed':
        call.status = 'completed';
        call.ended_at = new Date();
        if (dto.duration != null) {
          call.duration_seconds = dto.duration;
        } else if (dto.start_timestamp && dto.end_timestamp) {
          call.duration_seconds = Math.round((dto.end_timestamp - dto.start_timestamp) / 1000);
        }
        if (dto.recording_url) {
          call.recording_url = dto.recording_url;
        }
        break;
    }
    // Ensure contact/conversation are linked even if call was created earlier
    call.contact_id = contactId;
    call.conversation_id = conversationId;
    const saved = await this.callRepo.save(call);

import type { SupabaseClient, RealtimeChannel } from '@supabase/supabase-js';
export class RealtimeClient {
  private supabase: SupabaseClient;
  private channels = new Map<string, RealtimeChannel>();
  constructor(client: SupabaseClient) {
    this.supabase = client;
  }
  getOrCreate(name: string): RealtimeChannel {
    if (this.channels.has(name)) return this.channels.get(name)!;
    const ch = this.supabase.channel(name);
    this.channels.set(name, ch);
    return ch;
  }
  unsubscribe(name: string) {
    const ch = this.channels.get(name);
    if (ch) {
      ch.unsubscribe();
      this.channels.delete(name);
    }
  }
  broadcast(name: string, event: string, payload: unknown) {
    this.getOrCreate(name).send({ type: 'broadcast', event, payload });
  }
  unsubscribeAll() {
    this.channels.forEach((ch) => ch.unsubscribe());
    this.channels.clear();
  }
}

}

function contactNameFromCache(
  queryClient: ReturnType<typeof useQueryClient>,
  conversationId: string,
): string | undefined {
  const single = queryClient.getQueryData<Conversation>(['conversation', conversationId]);
  const fromSingle = formatContactName(single?.contact);
  if (fromSingle) return fromSingle;
  const lists = queryClient.getQueriesData<PaginatedResponse<Conversation>>({
    queryKey: ['conversations'],
  });
  for (const [, data] of lists) {
    const found = data?.items?.find((c) => c.id === conversationId);
    const name = formatContactName(found?.contact);
    if (name) return name;
  }
  return undefined;
}

  return name || undefined;

'use client';
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { useRealtime } from '@/providers/realtime-provider';
import type { StreamingPayload } from '@/types/realtime.types';
export function useRealtimeMessages(conversationId: string | null) {
  const { client } = useRealtime();
  const [streamingMessages, setStreamingMessages] = useState<Map<string, string>>(new Map());
  const [isStreaming, setIsStreaming] = useState(false);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!conversationId) return;
    const channelName = `conversation:${conversationId}`;
    const ch = client.getOrCreate(channelName);
    ch.on(
      'broadcast',
      { event: 'ai.response.streaming' },
      ({ payload }: { payload: StreamingPayload }) => {
        setStreamingMessages((prev) => {
          const next = new Map(prev);
          if (payload.isComplete) {
            next.delete(payload.messageId);
          } else {
            next.set(payload.messageId, payload.content);
          }
          setIsStreaming(next.size > 0);
          return next;
        });
      },
    ).subscribe();
    return () => {
      client.unsubscribe(channelName);
    };
  }, [conversationId, client]);
  return { streamingMessages, isStreaming };
}

import { useEffect, useRef, useState, useCallback } from 'react';
import { useRealtime } from '@/providers/realtime-provider';
import { useAuth } from '@/hooks/useAuth';
import type { TypingPayload } from '@/types/realtime.types';
export interface TypingUser {
  userId: string;
  userName: string;
  senderType: 'agent' | 'ai';
}
export function useTypingIndicator(conversationId: string | null) {
  const { client } = useRealtime();
  const { user } = useAuth();
  const [typingUsers, setTypingUsers] = useState<Map<string, TypingUser>>(new Map());
  const timers = useRef<Map<string, ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>>>(new Map());
  const sendDebounce = useRef<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null>(null);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!conversationId) return;
    const ch = client.getOrCreate(`conversation:${conversationId}`);
    const activeTimers = timers.current;
    const clearUser = (userId: string) => {
      setTypingUsers((prev) => {
        const n = new Map(prev);
        n.delete(userId);
        return n;
      });
      const t = timers.current.get(userId);
      if (t !== undefined) clearTimeout(t);
      timers.current.delete(userId);
    };
    ch.on('broadcast', { event: 'typing.started' }, ({ payload }: { payload: TypingPayload }) => {
      if (payload.userId === user?.id) return;
      setTypingUsers((prev) => new Map(prev).set(payload.userId, payload));
      const existing = timers.current.get(payload.userId);
      if (existing !== undefined) clearTimeout(existing);
      timers.current.set(payload.userId, setTimeout(() => clearUser(payload.userId), 3000));
    });
    ch.on('broadcast', { event: 'typing.stopped' }, ({ payload }: { payload: TypingPayload }) => {
      clearUser(payload.userId);
    });
    return () => {
      activeTimers.forEach(clearTimeout);
      activeTimers.clear();
    };
  }, [conversationId, client, user?.id]);
  const stopTyping = useCallback(() => {
    if (!conversationId || !user) return;
    if (sendDebounce.current) clearTimeout(sendDebounce.current);
    client.broadcast(`conversation:${conversationId}`, 'typing.stopped', {
      userId: user.id,
      userName: user.user_metadata?.full_name ?? user.email ?? '',
      senderType: 'agent',
      conversationId,
    } satisfies TypingPayload);
  }, [conversationId, client, user]);
  const sendTyping = useCallback(() => {
    if (!conversationId || !user) return;
    if (sendDebounce.current) clearTimeout(sendDebounce.current);
    client.broadcast(`conversation:${conversationId}`, 'typing.started', {
      userId: user.id,
      userName: user.user_metadata?.full_name ?? user.email ?? '',
      senderType: 'agent',
      conversationId,
    } satisfies TypingPayload);
    sendDebounce.current = setTimeout(() => stopTyping(), 3000);
  }, [conversationId, client, user, stopTyping]);
  return { typingUsers: Array.from(typingUsers.values()), sendTyping, stopTyping };
}
'use client';
import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { useRealtime } from '@/providers/realtime-provider';
import { useAuth } from '@/hooks/useAuth';
import type { PresenceUser } from '@/types/realtime.types';
export function usePresence(conversationId: string | null) {
  const { client } = useRealtime();
  const { user } = useAuth();
  const [presentUsers, setPresentUsers] = useState<PresenceUser[]>([]);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!conversationId) return;
    const ch = client.getOrCreate(`conversation:${conversationId}`);
    const myState: PresenceUser | null = user
      ? {
          userId: user.id,
          userName: user.user_metadata?.full_name ?? user.email ?? 'Agent',
          role: user.user_metadata?.role ?? 'agent',
          onlineAt: new Date().toISOString(),
        }
      : null;
    const syncPresence = () => {
      setPresentUsers(Object.values(ch.presenceState<PresenceUser>()).flat());
    };
    const channelState = ch.state;
    const alreadySubscribed =
      channelState === 'joined' || channelState === 'joining' || channelState === 'leaving';
    if (alreadySubscribed) {
      if (myState) void ch.track(myState);
    } else {
      ch.on('presence', { event: 'sync' }, syncPresence).subscribe(async (status) => {
        if (status === 'SUBSCRIBED' && myState) await ch.track(myState);
      });
    }
    return () => {
      void ch.untrack();
    };
  }, [conversationId, client, user]);
  return { presentUsers };
}

  notifyOrg(orgId: string, payload: InAppNotificationPayload): Promise<void> {
    return this.broadcastToOrg(orgId, 'notification.created', {
      id: payload.id ?? randomUUID(),
      type: payload.type,
      title: payload.title,
      description: payload.description,
      href: payload.href,
      conversationId: payload.conversationId,
      contactId: payload.contactId,

    });
  }
  async broadcastToOrg(orgId: string, event: string, payload: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<void> {
    await this.publish(`org:${orgId}`, event, payload);
  }
  async broadcastToConversation(conversationId: string, event: string, payload: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<void> {
    await this.publish(`conversation:${conversationId}`, event, payload);
  }
  private async publish(topic: string, event: string, payload: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<void> {
    if (!this.supabase) return;
    const viaHttp = await this.sendViaHttp(topic, event, payload);
    if (viaHttp) return;
    await this.sendViaSocket(topic, event, payload);
  }
  private async sendViaHttp(topic: string, event: string, payload: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<boolean> {
    try {
      const res = await fetch(`${this.supabaseUrl}/realtime/v1/api/broadcast`, {
        method: 'POST',
        headers: {
          'Content-Type': 'application/json',
          apikey: this.serviceKey,
          Authorization: `Bearer ${this.serviceKey}`,
        },
        body: JSON.stringify({
          messages: [{ topic, event, payload }],
        }),
      });
      if (!res.ok) {
        const body = await res.text();
        this.logger.warn(`Broadcast HTTP ${res.status} topic=${topic}: ${body}`);
        return false;
      }
      return true;
    } catch (err) {
      this.logger.warn(`Broadcast HTTP failed: ${(err as Error).message}`);
      return false;
    }
  }
  private async sendViaSocket(topic: string, event: string, payload: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<void> {
    if (!this.supabase) return;
    const channel = this.supabase.channel(topic, {
      config: { broadcast: { ack: true } },
    });
    try {
      await new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
        const timeout = setTimeout(() => reject(new Error('subscribe timeout')), 4000);
        channel.subscribe((status) => {
          if (status === 'SUBSCRIBED') {
            clearTimeout(timeout);
            resolve();
          }
          if (status === 'CHANNEL_ERROR' || status === 'TIMED_OUT' || status === 'CLOSED') {
            clearTimeout(timeout);
            reject(new Error(status));
          }
        });
      });
      const result = await channel.send({ type: 'broadcast', event, payload });
      if (result !== 'ok') {
        this.logger.warn(`Broadcast socket returned ${String(result)} topic=${topic}`);
      }
    } catch (err) {
      this.logger.warn(`Broadcast failed: ${(err as Error).message}`);
    } finally {
      await this.supabase.removeChannel(channel);
    }
  }
}

      queryClient.setQueryData(['messages', conversationId], ctx?.prev);
      toast({ title: 'Failed to send', variant: 'error' });

      // Refetch the thread so the persisted message replaces the optimistic one

      queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['messages', conversationId] });
      queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['conversations'] });
      // The open thread actually renders from contact-activity, not messages —
      // without this, a sent message only appears after the 4s poll catches up.
      if (contactId) {
        queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['contact-activity', contactId] });
      }
    },
  });
}
'use client';
import { useInfiniteQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import { activityService } from '@/services/activity.service';
export function useContactActivity(contactId: string | null) {
  return useInfiniteQuery({
    queryKey: ['contact-activity', contactId],
    queryFn: ({ pageParam }) =>
      activityService.getContactActivity(contactId!, pageParam as string | undefined),
    enabled: !!contactId,
    initialPageParam: undefined as string | undefined,
    getNextPageParam: (lastPage) => lastPage.next_cursor ?? undefined,
    // This is the query the open thread actually renders from — nothing else
    // reliably invalidates it (sending a message targets a separate
    // ['messages', conversationId] cache that this screen doesn't read), so
    // without polling, new messages never appear until a full remount.
    refetchInterval: 4000,
    refetchIntervalInBackground: false,
    refetchOnWindowFocus: true,
  });
}

  private getRecipientForChannel(contact: ContactEntity, channel: string): string | null {
    switch (channel) {
      case 'whatsapp':
        return contact.channel_ids?.whatsapp ?? null;
      case 'sms':
        return contact.phone ?? null;
      case 'email':
        return contact.email ?? null;
      case 'voice':
        return contact.channel_ids?.voice ?? contact.phone ?? null;
      case 'instagram':
        return contact.channel_ids?.instagram ?? null;
      case 'messenger':
        return contact.channel_ids?.messenger ?? null;
      default:
        return contact.channel_ids?.[channel] ?? null;
    }
  }
  private async orgHasActiveChannel(organizationId: string, type: string): Promise<boolean> {
    // SMS and email use global infrastructure (Telnyx/Resend) — no per-org channel entity needed
    if (type === 'email' || type === 'sms') return true;
    try {
      const channel = await this.channelsService.findActiveByType(organizationId, type);
      return !!channel;
    } catch {
      return false;
    }
  }
}

# Plan: Human handoff, composer, live calls, realtime, role security, human payment links, new channels
Follows `module-consolidation-investigation.md` and `contact-360-deep-dive.md`.
Everything below was checked against the code before planning. File references are given so each point can be verified.
No code has been changed yet.
Tags: 🟢 web only · 🟡 additive API (no existing behavior changes) · 🔴 **core / rule change, approved by the product owner in this round** · ❓ needs a product decision (a recommendation is given).
---
## 0. Product owner decisions (round 2) → workstreams
| Decision | Workstream |
|---|---|
| When a human takes over, the AI must **never** answer until control goes back to the AI | **WS1** Handoff = AI silence (🔴 approved) |
| Enforcement: don't send events to the integrations (n8n / ProSales) while a human has control. The textbox is locked while the AI has control and unlocked when a human does. | WS1.1 trigger guard, WS1.5 composer lock |
| Remove the "Reply via" picker | **WS2** Composer |
| Live-call banner: show "in progress", but Retell can't be followed live; results arrive at the end | **WS3** Live call state |
| Realtime: check the setup before changing anything, then plan | **WS4** Realtime (audit first) |
| AI agent, channels, webhooks and service prices are admin-only | **WS5** Role security (🔴 approved) |
| Humans can create payment links inside the conversation, **only while human intervention is on** | **WS6** Human payment links |
| Agents can resolve "payment needs attention" | WS5.4 (🔴 approved) |
| A new channel can be started when the contact already gave permission (e.g. started on Facebook, then gave a phone number) | **WS7** Start conversation on another channel |
---
## 1. Verified facts the plan depends on
### 1.1 Handoff today
| Fact | Where |
|---|---|
| `POST /conversations/:id/handoff` is a **toggle** (`bot_active = !bot_active`), not "set to human". A retry flips it back. | `conversation-management.service.ts:360-372` |
| The handoff event only feeds analytics. Nothing else listens to it. | `notifications/conversation-event.consumer.ts:62-77` |
| **3 producers** put AI trigger jobs on the queue: inbound messages, `call.completed` (Retell `call_ended`/`call_analyzed`), and `payment.received`/`payment.expired` | `conversation-management.service.ts:556`, `voice/calls.service.ts:180`, `payments/payments.service.ts:518` |
| The trigger processor never reads `bot_active`. It POSTs the event to the workflow endpoint. | `ai-automation/agent-trigger.processor.ts:61-200` |
| Replies reach the customer through `ConversationManagementService.sendMessage`, called from: the web/API controller (JWT user **or** API key), the AI tool `send_message`, and the follow-up handlers `send-message.handler.ts` / `call.handler.ts` | `grep .sendMessage(` (4 call sites) |
| `sendMessage` never sets `sender_type`, so AI replies, human replies and follow-ups are all stored as `'user'` (the column default). The thread can't show which replies came from the AI. | `conversation-management.service.ts:235-245`, `message.entity.ts:50` |
| API keys authenticate with `tenant.role = 'api_key'` | `tenant-context.middleware.ts:195-204` |
| New conversations default to `bot_active = true`. A resolved conversation + a new inbound message = a new open conversation with the AI on. | `014_contact_extensions.sql:11`, `findOrCreateActiveConversation` |
| A "hand over to a person" mechanism already exists for follow-up steps (`markAwaitingUser` + "Follow-up due" notification) | `automation-engine/action-execution.service.ts` (`handOver`), `action-execution.handover.spec.ts` |
### 1.2 Composer
| Fact | Where |
|---|---|
| "Reply via" only changes the badge and the template filter. The send always uses the current conversation. Its state carries over to the next conversation. | `components/inbox/message-composer.tsx:36,63-71` |
| Outbound dispatch exists only for WhatsApp, SMS, Facebook, Instagram. Voice and email text is saved and never delivered. | `conversation-management.service.ts:59-61` |
| When dispatch can't find a recipient (e.g. no `wa_id`) it just `return`s. The message stays `pending` forever, with no error shown. | `outbound-dispatch.processor.ts:64-90, 225-229` |
| The optimistic "sent" message is written to `['messages', id]`. The thread renders `['contact-activity', id]`, so there's no instant feedback. | `hooks/useMessages.ts:30-52`, `hooks/useContactActivity.ts` |
### 1.3 Calls (Retell)
| Fact | Where |
|---|---|
| Events handled: `call_started` → `status='in_progress'`, `started_at` set. `call_ended`/`call_analyzed` → `status='completed'`, plus duration, recording, summary. An outbound call is first inserted as `initiated`. `failed` is never written. | `voice/calls.service.ts:318-350` |
| The web listens for `status === 'active'`, a value the API never writes, so the banner can't show. It also only clears on `completed`. | `providers/realtime-provider.tsx:141-178` |
| The banner state only comes from realtime events. If you open the page mid-call, you see nothing. | same |
| The call detail page says "Live — refreshing every 5s" and polls transcripts. Per the product owner, transcripts only arrive at the end. | `app/(dashboard)/voice/[id]/page.tsx` |
### 1.4 Realtime, as the code uses it today
```
Browser (anon key + user session)
 ├─ channel org:<orgId>
 │   ├─ postgres_changes INSERT conversations.messages   filter organization_id=eq.<org>
 │   ├─ postgres_changes UPDATE conversations.conversations filter organization_id=eq.<org>
 │   ├─ postgres_changes INSERT/UPDATE voice.calls          filter organization_id=eq.<org>
 │   └─ broadcast notification.created   ← API (service role, HTTP /realtime/v1/api/broadcast)
 └─ channel conversation:<id>   (shared by 3 hooks)
     ├─ broadcast typing.started/stopped   (browser ↔ browser)
     ├─ presence sync                      (browser ↔ browser)
     └─ broadcast ai.response.streaming    ← no emitter found in this repo
React Query = source of truth; realtime = signal; polling = backstop
 (contact-activity every 4s, conversations list every 8s)
```
| Fact | Where |
|---|---|
| **The publication (`supabase_realtime`) and RLS policies are not in the repo.** They are configured in the Supabase project and can't be verified from code. | `packages/database/schemas/*.sql` (none) |
| The org filter is chosen by the client. It is **not a security boundary** unless RLS is enabled on the published tables. The provider comment documents an earlier cross-org leak. | `realtime-provider.tsx:56-66` |
| Broadcast channels are public: no `private: true` on the client or on the server broadcast | `realtime-client.ts`, `realtime-broadcast.service.ts` |
| `['conversation', id]` (singular) is patched on UPDATE, but the app reads `['conversations', id]`. Dead write. The broad invalidation still refetches. | `realtime-provider.tsx:130`, `hooks/useConversations.ts:20` |
| Every inbound message in the org invalidates **all** `contact-activity` queries, not just the open lead's | `realtime-provider.tsx:119` |
| Nothing pushes contact changes (stage moved by a rule, AI-captured data, score, insights). The panel goes stale. | no `clients.contacts` subscription or broadcast |
| The `conversation:<id>` channel is shared by typing, presence and streaming. `useRealtimeMessages` calls `subscribe()` without checking state, and its cleanup unsubscribes the channel for everyone. supabase-js throws if `subscribe()` is called twice on the same channel instance. **To confirm in a browser.** | `hooks/useRealtimeMessages.ts`, `usePresence.ts`, `useTypingIndicator.ts` |
| The org channel is subscribed without a status callback, so missed events aren't re-synced after a reconnect (polling hides it) | `realtime-provider.tsx:194` |
### 1.5 Roles and secrets
| Fact | Where |
|---|---|
| `@Roles` only on: calendars (writes), contact stage, users, billing, payment settings, payment attention | `grep @Roles` |
| **No guard on writes to:** AI agent config + capture fields, automation agents/tools, channels + WhatsApp sessions, webhooks, payment services (prices), **API keys**, ProSales integration, knowledge, sequence templates, funnels, communication templates, quick replies, branding, notification preferences | controllers listed in §WS5 |
| `@Roles(OWNER, ADMIN)` also blocks API keys (`'api_key'` isn't in the list). The calendar docs say "owner or admin key/user", but keys are rejected today. | `roles.guard.ts`, `ApiDocsSection.tsx` |
| **Secret exposure to any role:** `GET /channels` masks only exact keys `api_key, password, access_token, api_secret, auth_token, hmac_secret`. It returns `page_access_token` (Facebook/Instagram), `app_secret` and `verify_token` **unmasked**. | `integrations/channels.service.ts:13,57-64` |
| **Secret exposure to any role:** `GET /ai/agents` returns `auth_header_value`, the X-API-Key sent to the workflow endpoint | `ai-automation/automation-agents.controller.ts:28`, entity `:42` |
| Webhook `secret` is `select: false` (OK). ProSales `api_key` is stripped from `GET /organizations/me` (OK). | |
| The web shows Settings + Admin to agents. Only `/admin/*` has a redirect guard. `/config/funnel` (a work view) lives under `/config`. | `sidebar.tsx`, `admin/layout.tsx` |
### 1.6 Payments and channels
| Fact | Where |
|---|---|
| `POST /payments {contact_id, service_id, conversation_id?, booking?}` works for any role. `GET /payments/services` is open to all roles. | `payments.controller.ts`, `payment-service.controller.ts` |
| The payment row has **no `origin`** column. The origin goes only to the held appointment. "AI assisted revenue" uses the conversation's **current** `bot_active`. | `payments.service.ts:168,225-233`, `analytics.service.ts:~302` |
| Recipient per channel: WhatsApp (WAHA) needs `contact.channel_ids.whatsapp` (**no phone fallback**). SMS uses `contact.phone`. FB/IG need `psid`/`igsid`, which only exist after the contact writes first. Email and voice have no text dispatch. | `outbound-dispatch.processor.ts`, `channel-strategy-resolver.service.ts:165-181` |
| Opt-out = tag `opt-out` (AI tool `opt_out_contact`) + sequence cancellation on opt-out words. There is no explicit consent field. | `tool-execution.service.ts:354-380`, `conversation-management.service.ts:88-100,503` |

## WS1: Human handoff = AI silence (🔴 approved, core)
**Target behavior**
| State | AI receives events | AI replies accepted | Human textbox | Automated follow-ups |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **AI in control** (`bot_active = true`) | ✅ | ✅ | 🔒 locked: "The AI is handling this conversation · [Take over]" | run as today |
| **Human in control** (`bot_active = false`) | ❌ not sent to n8n/ProSales | ❌ rejected (late or in-flight replies) | ✏️ unlocked · [Return to AI] | ❓ D1: become "Your turn" tasks (recommended) |
### WS1.1 Trigger guard (🔴, API)
- In `AgentTriggerProcessor.process`, **before** the billing/agent lookup:
  - If `conversation_id` is set, load the conversation. If `bot_active === false`, log `agent_skipped_human_control` (existing `agentTriggerService.log`) and return.
  - If `conversation_id` is null (payment created without a conversation), check the contact's open conversations. If any is human-owned, skip. This keeps "human in control" lead-wide (see D2).
- Check at **processing** time, not when enqueuing, so jobs already in the queue when the human took over are dropped too.
- Applies to all 3 producers (message, call, payment) with no change in them.
### WS1.2 Reply guard (🔴, API)
- Add an `actor` to `sendMessage(conversationId, orgId, dto, actor)`: `{kind:'human', userId}` | `{kind:'ai'}` | `{kind:'automation'}`.
  - Controller: JWT user → `human`. `tenant.role === 'api_key'` → `ai` (integrations are the AI side per the product owner's rule).
  - Tool `send_message` → `ai`. Follow-up handlers → `automation`.
- Rules:
  - `human` + `bot_active = true` → **409 `AI_HAS_CONTROL`** (server-side mirror of the locked textbox).
  - `ai` + `bot_active = false` → **409 `HUMAN_HAS_CONTROL`**, logged as `reply_blocked_human_control`. This catches replies computed before the takeover.
  - `automation` + `bot_active = false` → D1.
- Update the API docs: `/conversations/:id/messages` now returns 409 for API keys while a human has control.
### WS1.3 Correct `sender_type` (🟡)
- `sendMessage` sets `sender_type` from the actor: `human → 'agent'` (+ `sender_id = userId`), `ai → 'ai'`, `automation → 'ai'` with `metadata.source = 'follow_up'`. Don't use `'system'`: the activity feed renders system messages as events, not bubbles.
- Effect: the thread can show "AI" vs "Ana (agent)" vs "Automated follow-up". Analytics only excludes `'system'`, so metrics are unchanged.
- Side effect to note: the AI's `get_conversation_history` tool maps `sender_type ?? direction` (`tool-execution.service.ts:293`). The AI will start seeing its own replies as `ai` instead of `user`. That's more accurate, but tell the ProSales/n8n owner.
- Existing rows stay `'user'`. An optional backfill isn't needed for the feature.
### WS1.4 Explicit, idempotent handoff (🟡)
- `POST /conversations/:id/handoff` accepts an optional body `{ bot_active: boolean }` that **sets** the value. Without a body it keeps the toggle behavior for existing n8n flows.
- The web always sends the explicit value, so two agents clicking at the same time can't flip it back.
- ❓ **D2, lead-level ownership (recommended: yes).** "Take over" / "Return to AI" apply to **all open conversations of the lead**. A conversation created while the lead is human-owned (a new inbound channel, or a human-started one in WS7) starts with `bot_active = false`. This is implemented in `findOrCreateActiveConversation` / `create`, with no schema change. Without it, a lead taken over on Facebook would get AI answers on WhatsApp.
- Notify on AI → human escalation: when `bot_active` goes to false from an API key (the AI escalating), call `realtime.notifyOrg` with "Lead X needs a human" (`href` to the inbox). Same pattern as the existing follow-up notifications.
### WS1.5 Composer lock and controls (🟢)
- The composer reads `bot_active` of the reply-target conversation:
  - AI in control: textarea disabled, banner "The AI is handling this conversation", primary button **Take over**.
  - Human in control: textarea enabled, secondary button **Return to AI**.
- Replace `AgentStatusToggle` (stale `useState`) with a controlled component based on the conversation query. Fixes B3.
- The lock updates live for other agents through the existing `conversations` UPDATE subscription. Fix the key (WS4.2) so it patches immediately instead of waiting for a refetch.
- Inbox list badge "👤 Human" and the "Needs human" view come from the same field.
### ❓ D1: automated follow-ups while a human has control
Recommended: in `ActionExecutionService.execute`, if the step's contact has a human-owned open conversation, call the **existing** `handOver(appt)`. The step becomes "Your turn" for the agent instead of sending. This reuses current behavior and shows up in the Today queue. The alternative (send anyway) breaks the "never answer" rule.
### WS1 tests
- `agent-trigger.processor.spec.ts` (new): skips on `bot_active=false` (message / call / payment with and without `conversation_id`); runs on `true`.
- `conversation-management.service.spec.ts`: 409 matrix for the actor × bot_active rules; `sender_type` per actor; explicit handoff is idempotent; toggle still works without a body; inheritance (D2).
- `action-execution.handover.spec.ts`: extend for D1.
- Web: composer locked/unlocked states; Take over / Return to AI send explicit values.

## WS2: Composer (🟢)
1. **Remove the "Reply via" picker** (and its `selectedChannel` state).
2. Show a read-only label instead: "Replying on **WhatsApp**". The target is:
   - inside a conversation row: that conversation;
   - in the lead-centric thread (deep-dive §4.2): the lead's conversation with the **latest inbound message**, or the latest open one if there's no inbound message.
3. Target channel with no dispatch (voice, email): composer disabled with a hint ("Voice conversations can't receive text. Use **Call**."). Webchat keeps working as today.
4. **Template button** filters by the target conversation's channel (it already takes a `channel` prop).
5. **Optimistic message into the rendered cache:** append the optimistic event to `['contact-activity', contactId]` (last page) and replace it on success. Drop the `['messages', id]` writes. `useMessages`/`conversation-timeline.tsx` are dead (B8).
6. **Delivery state (🟡 small):** add `status` to the activity `message` event (the column exists: pending/sent/failed) and show "Sending… / Sent / Not delivered". In dispatch, mark `failed` with a reason when the recipient can't be resolved, instead of a silent `return`. Today those messages look sent.

## WS3: Live call state (Retell) (🟢 + tiny 🟡)
**What we can know:** the call started, who with, which lead and conversation, how long it has been running (`started_at`), and that it ended. **What we can't know live:** transcript or content. Those arrive with `call_ended`/`call_analyzed`.
1. Realtime handlers: INSERT **or** UPDATE with `status === 'in_progress'` → add the active call; UPDATE to `completed` (or `failed`) → remove.
2. **Hydrate on load:** on mount, fetch `GET /voice/calls?limit=20` and keep rows with `in_progress` (UI-only). 🟡 Later, add a `status` filter to the endpoint.
3. **Stale guard:** if a call stays `in_progress` longer than N minutes (config, e.g. 60), show "Call status unknown: waiting for Retell" instead of a live badge. Lost webhooks happen.
4. **Banner copy** in the thread and on the lead row: "📞 Call in progress · handled by Retell AI · 03:12 · transcript and recording will appear when the call ends". The timer is computed client-side from `started_at`.
5. The call detail page replaces "Live — refreshing every 5s" with the same message and **stops polling** transcripts while `in_progress`. It refetches once on the `completed` event.
6. The composer on a voice target is disabled (WS2.3). The lead panel's **Call** button is disabled while a call is in progress for that lead.

## WS4: Realtime (audit first, then fix)
### WS4.0 Audit in the Supabase project (read-only, before any change)
Run in the SQL editor and attach the results to this plan:
```sql
-- 1. Which tables are published to Realtime
select schemaname, tablename from pg_publication_tables where pubname = 'supabase_realtime' order by 1,2;
-- 2. RLS on the published / candidate tables
select n.nspname, c.relname, c.relrowsecurity as rls_on, c.relforcerowsecurity as rls_forced, c.relreplident
from pg_class c join pg_namespace n on n.oid = c.relnamespace
where (n.nspname, c.relname) in (('conversations','messages'),('conversations','conversations'),('voice','calls'),('clients','contacts'));
-- 3. Policies on those schemas
select schemaname, tablename, policyname, roles, cmd, qual from pg_policies
where schemaname in ('conversations','voice','clients') order by 1,2;
-- 4. Broadcast/presence authorization (private channels)
select policyname, roles, cmd, qual, with_check from pg_policies where schemaname = 'realtime';
```
Also record from the dashboard: Realtime → Settings → "Allow public access" (channel restrictions), and whether the `conversations` and `voice` schemas are exposed.
**Decision gate.** If any published table has `rls_on = false`, or the policies don't restrict rows to the user's organization, **WS4.3 becomes priority 1**. In that case any holder of the public anon key could subscribe with another org's filter.
### WS4.1 Principles (keep)
Realtime is only a **signal**. Data always comes from REST/React Query. Polling stays as a backstop (you can lengthen it once signals are reliable). Ephemeral state (typing, presence, live call) is the only thing rendered straight from realtime.
### WS4.2 Client fixes (🟢, no infra change)
1. **Lead-scoped invalidation:** keep a `conversation_id → contact_id` map from the conversations cache. On message INSERT, invalidate only `['contact-activity', contactId]` and `['conversations']` (fall back to broad if unknown).
2. **Panel freshness without server changes:** when the open lead's activity returns a new `contact_data_updated` or `funnel_change` event (newer than the last one seen), invalidate `['contacts', id]` and `['captured-fields', id]`. Freshness ≤ 4s using the existing poll.
3. **Fix the key mismatch:** patch `['conversations', id]` (not `['conversation', id]`) on conversation UPDATE, so the composer lock and owner chips update at once. Fix `contactNameFromCache` the same way.
4. **One manager for `conversation:<id>`:** ref-count subscribers in `RealtimeClient` (`acquire`/`release`). `subscribe()` once; unsubscribe when the last hook releases. Fixes the double-subscribe risk and the early teardown.
5. **Resync on reconnect:** pass a status callback to `ch.subscribe()`. On `SUBSCRIBED` after `CHANNEL_ERROR`/`TIMED_OUT`/`CLOSED`, invalidate `['conversations']`, the open lead's activity and active calls.
6. **`ai.response.streaming`:** there's no emitter in this repo. Confirm with the ProSales/n8n owner whether they broadcast it. If not, remove the streaming bubble path.
7. WS3 handlers (calls).
### WS4.3 Server push and security (🟡 + Supabase config, after the audit)
1. **`contact.updated` broadcast** (🟡): after `update`, `updateCapturedData`, `updateStage`, `moveStageIfUnchanged` and the AI-insights write in `ClientManagementService`, call `realtimeBroadcast.broadcastToOrg(orgId, 'contact.updated', { contact_id, fields: [...] })`. The web invalidates that lead's queries. It's preferred over publishing `clients.contacts`: the payload is server-controlled, and no PII flows through `postgres_changes`.
2. **Private channels:** create `realtime.messages` policies that allow `org:<id>` and `conversation:<id>` topics only to members of that org. Subscribe with `{ config: { private: true } }` on the client, and send private broadcasts from the API. Notifications carry contact names and message previews.
3. **RLS on published tables** (if the audit shows gaps): a `SELECT` policy on `conversations.messages`, `conversations.conversations` and `voice.calls`, where `organization_id` equals the caller's org (looked up from `core.users` by `auth.uid()`).
4. Add the publication and policies to `packages/database/schemas/` as a migration, so they're versioned and stop living only in the dashboard.

Add `@Roles(UserRole.OWNER, UserRole.ADMIN)` to **mutating** routes. Keep `GET` routes open where agents need the data (e.g. payment services for the payment-link dialog, capture-field labels for the panel, channel list for badges).
| Area (product owner) | Routes to guard | API keys? |
|---|---|---|
| **AI agent** | `ai-agents`: `config/provision`, `config/from-brief`, `PUT config/*`, `POST /`, `PATCH :id`, `activate`, `deactivate`, capture-fields `POST/PATCH/DELETE/reorder` · `ai/agents` `POST/PATCH/DELETE` · `ai/tools` `POST` | no |
| **Channels** | `channels` `POST`, `POST :id/test`, `PATCH :id`, `PATCH :id/deactivate`, `DELETE :id` · `channels/whatsapp` `sessions`, `pairing-code`, `relink`, `unlink` | no |
| **Webhooks** | `webhooks` `POST`, `POST :id/test`, `PATCH :id`, `DELETE :id` | no |
| **Service prices** | `payments/services` `POST`, `PATCH :id`, `DELETE :id` | no |
Strongly recommended in the same change (credentials / org-level). ❓ Confirm:
| Area | Routes |
|---|---|
| API keys | `api-keys` `GET`, `POST`, `DELETE` (today an agent can create a key) |
| ProSales integration | `PATCH organizations/me/prosales-integration` |
| Branding / notifications / org sequence switch | `PATCH organizations/me/branding`, `me/notifications`, `me/sequences` |
❓ Also to decide (agents may legitimately edit some of these): knowledge base writes, sequence templates (`automation/sequences/templates*`), funnels and stages config, quick replies (`templates`), communication templates. Note: knowledge `POST` and communication templates are **documented for API keys** (`ApiDocsSection.tsx`), so if they are guarded they need the API-key allowance below.
**API-key handling:** extend the decorator as `@Roles(OWNER, ADMIN, { allowApiKey: true })` (or a separate `@AllowApiKey()`), and use it where the public API contract requires it. Also fix the calendar docs/behavior mismatch (docs promise "admin key"; keys are rejected today). ❓ Decide which is right.
### WS5.2 Stop leaking secrets (🔴 security fix, do with WS5.1)
- `ChannelsService.maskConfig`: add `page_access_token`, `app_secret`, `verify_token`. Better: mask any key matching `/(token|secret|password|key)$/i`. Keep `***` as the "unchanged" sentinel on PATCH (check the update path doesn't overwrite real values with `***`).

## WS6: Human payment links inside the conversation
**Rule (product owner):** a human can create a payment link in a conversation **only while human intervention is on**. The AI keeps creating links through its tool while it has control.
### Flow (🟢 web, existing endpoints)
1. The composer toolbar and the lead panel action bar get **💳 Payment link**. It's enabled only when the target conversation has `bot_active = false`. Tooltip otherwise: "Take over the conversation to send a payment link".
2. Dialog: pick a service (`GET /payments/services`, active ones). If the service's calendar charges at booking, offer the optional slot picker (reuse `SlotPicker` / the `booking` DTO, the same flow the appointment drawer already uses).
3. `POST /payments { contact_id, service_id, conversation_id, booking? }`.
4. The link is **inserted into the composer draft** ("Here is your payment link for *Consultation* (€50): <url>"). The human reviews and sends it. No automatic send, consistent with manual control.
5. The payment shows up in the lead panel (Payments, Next), pending.
### API side
- 🔴 (part of WS1 rules, approved) **Server-side check:** `POST /payments` from a **JWT user** with a `conversation_id` whose `bot_active = true` → 409 `AI_HAS_CONTROL`. API keys and the AI tool are unaffected.
- 🟡 **Record origin:** store `metadata.origin = 'human'` and `metadata.created_by = userId` on the payment (additive, jsonb). The AI tool path sets `'ai'`.
- 🟡 **Timeline event:** add `payment` events to `GET /contacts/:id/activity` (created / paid / expired, with amount, service, origin). The thread then shows "💳 €50 link sent by Ana · Paid ✓".
- **When it's paid:** `payment.received` triggers the AI. With WS1.1, if the human still has control the AI stays silent. Add an in-app notification to the org: "💳 Ana García paid €50, you're handling this conversation".
### ❓ D3: the "AI-assisted revenue" definition
Today it counts paid payments whose conversation **currently** has `bot_active = true`. A human-created link, paid after "Return to AI", would be counted as AI revenue.
Recommendation: change the `pay_ai_cur` query to also require `coalesce(p.metadata->>'origin','ai') <> 'human'`. Historic rows with no origin keep being treated as AI, so nothing changes for existing data. This is a metric definition change and needs a yes.
---
## WS7: Start a conversation on another channel
**Rule (product owner):** allowed when the contact already gave permission, e.g. started on Facebook and then gave a phone number.
### What's technically possible today
| Target channel | Recipient needed | Available after "gave phone"? | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SMS** | `contact.phone` | ✅ | Works with the existing dispatch |
| **WhatsApp (WAHA)** | `contact.channel_ids.whatsapp` | ❌ today, **no phone fallback** | 🔴 Needs a dispatch change: derive the chat id from `contact.phone` (`WahaService.toChatId(digits)`). Optionally verify the number is on WhatsApp first (WAHA has a "check exists" API; confirm it's available in your version). |
| **Voice** | `channel_ids.voice` or `phone` | ✅ | Already covered by the **Call** action (`POST /voice/calls`) |
| **Facebook / Instagram** | `psid` / `igsid` | ❌ | Only the contact can start it (platform rule). Not offered. |
| **Email** | `contact.email` | – | There's no conversational email dispatch. Out of scope. |
### Permission rule (❓ D4, recommended)
A channel is **offered** when all of these hold:
1. the recipient exists (table above);
2. the org has that channel active (same check as `ChannelStrategyResolver.orgHasActiveChannel`);
3. the contact is **not** tagged `opt-out`;
4. the agent confirms in the dialog: "The contact gave permission to be contacted on this number". The confirmation is recorded on the new conversation's `metadata.consent = { confirmed_by, at, source_channel }`.
Optional stricter variant: require that the phone was provided inside a conversation (a `contact_data_updated` event for `phone`), not typed in by staff.
### Implementation
- 🟡 `GET /contacts/:id/reachable-channels`: read-only. Reuses `ChannelStrategyResolver.getRecipientForChannel` + `orgHasActiveChannel` + opt-out → `[{channel, reachable, reason?}]`.
- 🟡 `POST /contacts/:id/conversations { channel, consent_confirmed: true }`: validates the rule above, then uses `findOrCreateActiveConversation`. Per D2, it creates the conversation with `bot_active = false` (the human started it, so the human owns it). Returns the conversation.
- 🔴 WhatsApp dispatch phone fallback (above). Also mark the message `failed` with a reason when no recipient can be resolved (WS2.6).
- 🟢 UI: the lead panel's channel chips show reachable channels as "+ WhatsApp". Clicking opens the consent dialog, creates the conversation, and focuses the composer on it. Unreachable channels show the reason on hover ("No phone number", "Contact opted out", "Only the contact can start Instagram").
### WS7 tests
- Reachable channels: opt-out, missing phone, inactive channel, FB/IG never offered.
- Create conversation: consent required; inherits human ownership; 409 when opted out.
- Dispatch: WhatsApp via phone fallback; `failed` status when unresolvable.

## 2. Order, dependencies, effort
| Phase | Content | Why first | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|
| **P0: Audit and security** | WS4.0 audit · WS5.2 secret masking · WS5.1 guards (4 confirmed areas + API keys) · WS5.3 nav/route guard | Exposed tokens and unguarded writes are live risks. The audit result decides the WS4.3 priority. | S–M |
| **P1: Handoff core** | WS1.1 · WS1.2 · WS1.3 · WS1.4 (explicit set + D2 if approved) · WS1.5 · D1 | The product's central promise ("AI never answers after a takeover") | M |
| **P2: Composer and calls** | WS2 · WS3 · WS4.2 client fixes | The inbox becomes reliable and honest about state | M |
| **P3: Human payments** | WS6 (+ D3) · WS5.4 | Depends on P1 (lock state and server check) | S–M |

I checked each of your points against the code and wrote the plan to .claude/plans/inbox-handoff-realtime-security-plan.md. No code has changed yet.


Two security issues to fix first, because they're exposed today:


Facebook/Instagram page tokens are visible to any logged-in user. GET /channels hides only a fixed list of field names, and the real token field (page_access_token) isn't on it. Nor are app_secret and verify_token.
The AI workflow's API key is visible to any role. GET /ai/agents returns the key the CRM sends to n8n/ProSales.

Agents can also create API keys.


How each of your points maps to the plan:


Human takeover means the AI stays silent. Three things send messages to n8n/ProSales: incoming messages, finished Retell calls, and payment events. None of them checks whether a human has control. The plan:
Check that flag when each queued job runs, so jobs already waiting when the human took over are dropped too.
Reject AI replies that arrive after a takeover.
Lock the textbox while the AI has control, and also reject human sends on the server.
I also found that every outbound message is saved as 'user', so the thread can't tell AI replies from human ones; the plan fixes that. Handoff is also a toggle today, so a retry can flip it back; the plan adds an explicit "set to human / set to AI" option.
"Reply via" picker: removed. It was only cosmetic. It's replaced by a read-only "Replying on WhatsApp" label, and voice/email conversations are disabled because they can't receive text.
Live-call banner: Retell does tell us when a call starts and ends, just not the content. The banner never shows today because it waits for a status of active, which the API never writes. The plan shows "Call in progress · handled by Retell AI · 03:12 · transcript when the call ends". It also loads active calls when the page opens, handles lost end-of-call webhooks, and stops the fake "live" transcript refresh.
Realtime: step 0 is a read-only audit. Which tables are published and which row-level security rules apply are configured in the Supabase project, not in the repo, so I couldn't check them. The plan includes the exact SQL to run. If those tables aren't restricted per organization, another organization's data could be received, and that becomes the top priority. Fixes that need no infrastructure change are listed separately, including two cache-key mismatches and a shared channel that can be closed for everyone when one component leaves.
Admin-only settings: the plan lists every write endpoint for AI agent, channels, webhooks and service prices. Reads stay open where agents need them. One catch: API keys authenticate with their own role, so a plain admin check also blocks n8n/ProSales keys. The plan adds an explicit allowance where the public API needs it.

Your answers to my questions:


Human payment links: a 💳 button in the conversation, enabled only while a human has control. It inserts the link into the draft for the agent to send. When the customer pays, the AI stays silent and the agent gets a notification.
Agents resolving payment attention: a role change on two endpoints.
Starting a new channel: SMS works today from the phone number. WhatsApp does not: sending needs a WhatsApp ID, not the phone number, so it needs a small core change. Facebook and Instagram can't be started by us at all; only the contact can start them. The plan also fixes messages that currently stay "pending" forever with no error.

Order: security and audit, then the takeover core, then composer/calls/realtime, then human payment links, then new channels.


Decisions I need from you:


D1: If a follow-up is due while a human has control, should it become a "Your turn" task instead of sending? I recommend yes.
D2: Should a takeover apply to all of the lead's channels, so a lead taken over on Facebook isn't answered by the AI on WhatsApp? I recommend yes.
D3: Payments are counted as "AI-assisted revenue" based on whether the AI is on in that conversation right now. A human-created link paid after returning control to the AI would be counted as AI revenue. Should human-created links be excluded?
D4: What counts as "permission" to start a channel? I suggest: the contact is not opted out, plus the agent confirms and that confirmation is recorded.
D5: Which other settings become admin-only (knowledge, sequences, funnels, quick replies, communications)?
D6: The docs say API keys can write calendars, but the code blocks them. Which one is right?
D7: Should payment-attention emails also go to agents, or in-app only?

ws8='''## WS8: Per-channel opt-out (✅ D4)

**Rule:** if the contact opts out, the CRM stops contacting them **on that channel**. Other channels remain possible.

### Today
| Mechanism | Scope | Where |
|---|---|---|
| AI tool `opt_out_contact` | adds contact-wide tag `opt-out` and cancels all sequences | `tool-execution.service.ts:354-380` |
| Opt-out words in an inbound message (regex) | cancels the active sequence only, no tag | `conversation-management.service.ts:88-100,503-505` |
| Tag `opt-out` | stops new sequences from being created | `outbound-message.consumer.ts:109-112` |
| **Sending** (human, AI, follow-ups, new conversations) | **not blocked at all** | – |

### Design (no schema change)
- **Storage:** contact tags `opt-out:<channel>` (e.g. `opt-out:whatsapp`). They're visible and removable in the lead panel, like any tag, so a human can reverse them. The legacy `opt-out` tag keeps its meaning: **all channels**.
- One helper, `isOptedOut(contact, channel)`: `tags includes 'opt-out' || tags includes 'opt-out:'+channel`.
- **Recording the opt-out:**
  - 🔴 AI tool `opt_out_contact`: when called with a `conversation_id` (the execute DTO already carries it), tag `opt-out:<that conversation's channel>` instead of the global tag. Without a conversation, keep the global `opt-out`. It still cancels the contact's sequences, as today (conservative).
  - 🟢 Lead panel: the channel chip menu gets "Mark opted out on WhatsApp" (adds the tag). Removing the tag reverses it.
  - Regex detection of opt-out words keeps its current effect (cancel sequence) and **does not** tag. It matches phrases like "no quiero…" in normal sentences, so tagging from it would silently block legitimate contacts.
- **Enforcement (🔴, approved by D4).** Every path that contacts the lead checks `isOptedOut(contact, channel)`:

| Path | Behavior when opted out on that channel |
|---|---|
| `sendMessage` (human, AI, API key, follow-up) | 409 `CHANNEL_OPTED_OUT`. The message isn't stored or dispatched. |
| AI trigger (WS1.1) | skipped, logged `agent_skipped_opted_out` |
| Follow-up channel resolver | skips that channel. `auto` strategy picks the next reachable channel; `*_only` on that channel → the step is handed over as "Your turn" with the reason |
| Outbound call (`POST /voice/calls`) | blocked when opted out on `voice` (or globally) |
| WS7 start conversation | channel not offered / 409 |

- Inbound messages on an opted-out channel are still received and shown. The composer on that channel is disabled: "Ana opted out of WhatsApp · remove the opt-out to contact her again".

### Tests
- `isOptedOut` matrix (global vs per-channel tag).
- `sendMessage` 409 for each actor. Resolver skip and hand-over. Tool tags the conversation's channel. Call blocked.

---

'''

I've added all seven decisions to .claude/plans/inbox-handoff-realtime-security-plan.md; the plan is final and no product decisions are left open. No code has changed.


What each decision changes:


Decision    Change to the plan
D1 Follow-ups become "Your turn" tasks    A follow-up that falls due while a human has control isn't sent. It reuses the existing mechanism that turns a step into a "Your turn" task with a notification.
D2 Ownership per lead    Take over / Return to AI applies to every open conversation of the lead, through a new single endpoint (POST /contacts/:id/handoff). When n8n/ProSales escalates one conversation, that also applies to the whole lead. A conversation that opens while the lead is human-owned starts human-owned. Once all of a lead's conversations are resolved, the next incoming message goes back to the AI.
D3 Human links don't count as AI    Human-created payment links are marked as human and excluded from "AI-assisted revenue". Older payments keep today's treatment.
D4 No consent tracking, opt-out per channel    No permission dialog. A channel can be started if the contact is reachable on it, your org has that channel active, and they haven't opted out of it. Opt-out gets its own workstream (below).
D5 Only the 4 areas    Owner/admin only for AI agent, channels, webhooks and service prices. Read access stays open where agents need it, for example the services list for payment links. Agents keep Settings with only the unprotected pages. The two secret leaks are still fixed because they belong to channels and AI agent.
D6 API keys can't write calendars    The code stays as it is. Only the API docs change, to say API keys get a 403 on calendar writes. None of the 4 protected areas is used by API keys, so no special allowance is needed.
D7 In-app only    Nothing to change. The in-app notification already reaches everyone in the org, and only admins get the email.

Per-channel opt-out (new workstream). Today opt-out is contact-wide, and nothing actually stops messages from going out to an opted-out contact.


How it's stored: a tag per channel, for example opt-out:whatsapp. It's visible in the lead panel, and an agent can remove it to reverse it. The existing opt-out tag keeps meaning "all channels".
How it's set: when the AI's opt-out tool is used inside a conversation, it tags that conversation's channel. An agent can also mark it by hand. The automatic detection of words like "no quiero" keeps only cancelling the sequence and doesn't tag. It matches normal sentences too often, so tagging from it would block real leads.
Where it's enforced: messages from anyone on that channel are rejected, the AI isn't triggered, follow-ups skip that channel (or become "Your turn"), outbound calls are blocked, and the channel can't be started. Incoming messages on that channel are still received and shown.

Order:


P0: security fixes, the Supabase audit and the docs.
P1: takeover core.
P2: composer, calls and realtime fixes.
P3: human payment links, and agents resolving payment attention.
P4: opt-out, then new channels.
P5: live contact updates and private realtime channels, moved earlier if the audit finds gaps.

Two things need other people, not product decisions:


Whoever owns the n8n/ProSales workflows needs notice of behavior changes that affect them:
AI replies are rejected (409) while a human has control.
A handoff now applies to the whole lead.
The AI's own past replies show as ai in the conversation history it reads.
The opt-out tool now tags only the conversation's channel.
I also need them to say whether they send the "AI response streaming" event. Nothing in this repo sends it.
Whoever administers the Supabase project needs to run the audit queries in the plan. Which tables are published and the row-level security (RLS) rules can't be checked from the code.

If you want me to start implementing, P0 is the natural first step; the secret masking and the four admin guards are small, self-contained changes.

file_text:

# Master Plan: Inbox-first CRM (UI + platform)
**This is the single plan to implement from.** It merges:
- `module-consolidation-investigation.md`: module consolidation, navigation, benchmark (round 1)
- `contact-360-deep-dive.md`: Contact 360 / lead panel design (round 2)
- `inbox-handoff-realtime-security-plan.md`: handoff, realtime, security, payments, channels (rounds 2–3)
Where those documents disagree, **this one wins**. The others stay as evidence: file references, verified facts, benchmark.
No code has been changed yet.
Tags: 🟢 web only · 🟡 additive API · 🔴 core/rule change (approved) · 👤 agent-visible · 🛡️ admin-only
---
## 1. Principles
1. **The Inbox is the workspace.** Agents live there. Every other screen either feeds it or is configuration.
2. **The lead is the unit of work.** One lead can arrive through several channels, but it is one row, one thread, one panel.
3. **One source of truth per decision.** Every decision about a lead (owner, stage, data, booking, payment, follow-up, opt-out) has exactly one control, in the Lead panel, and it looks the same everywhere.
4. **AI or human, never both.** While the AI has control, humans watch. While a human has control, the AI is silent. Control is per lead.
5. **Everything is linked.** Any contact, call, appointment or payment shown anywhere opens in context (peek drawer), not on a dead-end page.
6. **Operations vs configuration.** Daily work lives in the main navigation. Setup lives in Settings, and the sensitive parts are admin-only.
---
## 2. Decision log (all rounds)
| # | Topic | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| R1-1 | Voice placement | **Recommendation adopted:** voice is a channel of the lead. Calls live in the thread and in an Inbox **Calls** view, and `/voice` leaves the main nav. *(No objection was raised. Reverting it is a nav-only change.)* |
| R1-2 | Work style | Inbox-first, lead-centric, decisions centralized |
| R1-3 | Agents and payments | Agents see and manage payments day-to-day |
| R1-4 | Companies | Out of scope. The super-admin org/subscription list is parked. |
| R2-1 | Human handoff | While a human has control the AI never answers, until control is returned |
| R2-2 | Enforcement | Don't send events to n8n/ProSales while a human has control. Textbox locked while the AI has control. |
| R2-3 | "Reply via" picker | Removed |
| R2-4 | Live calls | Show "in progress". Content only arrives when the Retell call ends. |
| R2-5 | Realtime | Audit first, then fix |
| R2-6 | Security | AI agent, channels, webhooks, service prices are admin-only |
| R2-7 | Human payment links | Allowed inside the conversation, only while a human has control |
| R2-8 | Agents resolve payment attention | Yes |
| R2-9 | Start a conversation on another channel | Yes, when the contact is reachable there |
| D1 | Follow-up due while a human has control | It becomes a **"Your turn"** task |
| D2 | Ownership scope | **Per lead** (all channels) |
| D3 | Human-created payment links | Don't count as AI-assisted revenue |
| D4 | Consent | Not tracked. **Opt-out is per channel**: stop contacting on that channel |
| D5 | Guarded settings | Only the 4 areas in R2-6 |
| D6 | API keys writing calendars | Not allowed (code stays, docs are fixed) |
| D7 | Payment attention for agents | In-app notification only |
---
## 3. Target experience: navigation and roles
### 3.1 Navigation: before → after
```
TODAY                                        AFTER
Main:     Dashboard                          Home          Today queue + KPIs             👤
          Inbox                              Inbox         Leads · views · Calls view     👤
          Contacts                           Contacts      Table | Pipeline (ex-Funnel)   👤
          Funnel (/config/funnel)            Schedule      appointments + follow-ups      👤
          Voice                              Payments      transactions + attention       👤
          Schedule
Settings: AI Agent, Sequences, Templates,    Settings (grouped, filtered by role)
          Webhooks, Channels,                  AI Agent         agent, knowledge, routing     🛡️
          Communications, Payments             Automation       funnels & stages, sequences   👤
                                               Messaging        quick replies, notifications  👤
                                               Payments setup   Stripe, services & prices     🛡️
                                               Connections      channels, webhooks, API keys  🛡️
Admin:    Panel, Team, Billing, API Keys     Admin: Team, Billing                             🛡️
Hidden:   /integrations (mock)               removed → redirect to Connections
```
Old routes keep working through redirects:
| Old route | New route |
|---|---|
| `/` | Home |
| `/voice` | `/inbox?view=calls` |
| `/voice/:id` | opens the call drawer |
| `/config/funnel` | `/contacts?view=pipeline` |
| `/config/payments` | Payments setup (transactions move to `/payments`) |
| `/integrations` | Connections |
| `/templates` | Settings › Messaging › Quick replies |
### 3.2 What each role sees
| Area | Agent 👤 | Admin/Owner 🛡️ |
|---|---|---|
| Home, Inbox, Contacts, Schedule, Payments | ✅ | ✅ |
| Settings › Automation, Messaging | ✅ | ✅ |
| Settings › AI Agent, Payments setup, Connections | hidden, and the API returns 403 on writes | ✅ |
| Admin (Team, Billing) | hidden (it already redirects today) | ✅ |
| Resolve payment attention | ✅ (R2-8) | ✅ |
| Book outside calendar rules, delete appointments | ❌ (existing API rule) | ✅ |
One `usePermissions()` hook drives the sidebar, ⌘K, the page guards and the action buttons.
---
## 4. Target experience: the Inbox
### 4.1 Layout
```
┌────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────┐
│ LEAD LIST          │ THREAD                               │ LEAD PANEL (§5)      │
│ Views:             │ Ana García · [WA][SMS] · 🤖 AI       │                      │
│  Needs human (3)   │ [All][Messages][Calls][Appts][Pay]   │                      │
│  Your turn (2)     │  [Stage][Data]   ← filter chips      │                      │
│  Unread (5)        │                                      │                      │
│  Hot · AI active   │  …unified timeline, all channels…    │                      │
│  All open·Resolved │  each bubble: channel badge +        │                      │
│  Calls             │  author (AI / Ana / Follow-up)       │                      │
│ [search leads…]    │                                      │                      │
│ ─────────────────  │ 📞 Call in progress · Retell · 03:12 │                      │
│ (AG) Ana García    │                                      │                      │
│  [WA][SMS]      5m │ ┌──────────────────────────────────┐ │                      │
│  "¿Tenéis cita…"   │ │ composer (state depends on §4.3) │ │                      │
│  🔥 👤 📅 💳     ② │ └──────────────────────────────────┘ │                      │
└────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────┘
```
### 4.2 Lead list
| Change | Detail | Tag |
|---|---|---|
| **One row per lead** | Avatar, name, icons of the channels with open conversations, latest message across channels, total unread, badges: 🔥 hot, 👤 human has control, 📅 appointment today, 💳 pending payment, 📞 call in progress | 🟢 interim (group the loaded page) → 🟡 `GET /inbox/leads` |
| **Views** (saved filters, kept in the URL) | Needs human · Your turn · Unread · Hot · AI active · All open · Resolved · **Calls** | 🟢 (`status`, `assigned_to` already exist in the API) |
| **Search that works** | Name, phone, email | 🟡 the API ignores `search` today |
| Pin | Kept | – |
| Live updates | Lead-scoped invalidation, resync after a reconnect | 🟢 |
### 4.3 Composer: one component, five states
| State | When | What the agent sees |
|---|---|---|
| **AI has control** | lead `bot_active = true` | Textbox 🔒 locked. "🤖 The AI is handling this lead" · **[Take over]** |
| **Human has control** | lead `bot_active = false` | Textbox enabled. Read-only label "Replying on **WhatsApp**" (the channel of the last inbound message). Toolbar: Quick reply · **💳 Payment link** · Send. **[Return to AI]** |
| **Opted out** | the target channel is opted out | Disabled: "Ana opted out of WhatsApp · remove the opt-out to contact her" |
| **No text channel** | target is voice/email | Disabled: "This channel can't receive text · use **Call**" |
| **Sending / failed** | after Send | Bubble shows "Sending… / Sent / Not delivered (reason)" |
The "Reply via" picker is removed (R2-3). The optimistic message appears in the thread immediately (it's written into the cache the thread actually renders).
### 4.4 Thread
- It stays lead-wide, as it is today. New: **filter chips** by event type. **Author labels** (AI / agent name / Automated follow-up) once `sender_type` is stored correctly.
- **Clickable events:** call → call drawer (recording, transcript). Appointment → appointment drawer. Payment → payment row. Stage/data change → opens the panel section.
- **New event types** 🟡: payment (created / paid / expired, "link sent by Ana"), follow-up step (sent / handed over).
- **Live call banner** (R2-4): "📞 Call in progress · handled by Retell AI · 03:12 · transcript and recording will appear when the call ends". A timer runs from `started_at`. If it's stuck, the banner says "waiting for Retell".
- **Header:** lead name, channel chips, the owner toggle (same control as the panel), and Resolve (resolves the lead's open conversations, so the lead returns to the AI on the next inbound message, per D2).
### 4.5 Calls view (replaces the Voice page)
- The Inbox view **Calls**: a table of calls with lead chip, direction, status, duration, started. Filters: status, direction 🟡 (the API only supports limit/offset today).
- Row → call drawer (metadata, recording, transcript, "Open lead").

One component, `LeadPanel`, used in 3 places: the **Inbox right column**, the **`/contacts/[id]` workspace** (§6.1), and the **peek drawer** (§6.2). It replaces the contact profile page cards, the inbox contact sidebar, the funnel quick-view dialog, and the unused `contact-profile-panel.tsx`.

### 5.1 Section rules
| Section | Rule | Data (existing unless tagged) |
|---|---|---|
| A Identity | Copy phone/email. Channel chip states: active ✓, opted out ⊘ (WS8), reachable "+" (WS7), unreachable (reason on hover). "Created by AI / manually" replaces the misleading "Handling mode". | contact, `/contacts/:id/messages`, 🟡 `/contacts/:id/reachable-channels` |
| B Decisions | **Owner is one lead-level toggle** (D2), not per channel. Stage uses a single shared hook. Score is read-only. | 🟡 `POST /contacts/:id/handoff`, `PATCH /contacts/:id/stage` |
| C Actions | Message focuses the composer (or opens the Inbox when in a drawer). Call: `POST /voice/calls`, disabled during a live call or if opted out of voice. Book: appointment drawer pre-filled with the contact. Payment link: only while a human has control. Follow-up: start a sequence. | existing |
| D Next | Shows only what exists. Empty = nothing pending. | appointments, `/payments?contact_id=`, sequences |
| E Qualification | Labels from the agent's capture fields. Hide the bookkeeping keys. Edits go through `/captured-data` (keeps scoring and funnel rules). | existing |
| F AI summary | Also shown on the full workspace (missing today) | contact `ai_insights` |
| G Related | Collapsed by default, fetched when opened, counts in the header | existing endpoints |
| H Details | Inline edit, tags, and the list of per-channel opt-outs (add/remove) | existing + WS8 tags |
### 5.2 Freshness
The panel updates within ~4s when the AI captures data or a rule moves the stage (client fix first). Later, the server broadcasts a `contact.updated` event (🟡).

import path from 'path';
const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  // Visual regression tests build into their own directory (see playwright.config.ts).
  distDir: process.env.NEXT_DIST_DIR || '.next',
  output: 'standalone',
  outputFileTracingRoot: path.join(__dirname, '../../'),
  transpilePackages: ['@crm/shared'],
  images: {
    remotePatterns: [
      {
        protocol: 'https',
        hostname: '**.supabase.co',
      },
    ],
  },
  async rewrites() {
    const apiBase = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3001';
    return [
      {
        source: '/api/:path*',
        destination: `${apiBase.replace(/\/api\/?$/, '')}/:path*`,
      },
    ];

export default nextConfig;
import { createServerClient, type CookieOptions } from '@supabase/ssr';
import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server';
const PUBLIC_PATHS = ['/login', '/signup'];
const OPEN_PATHS = ['/accept-invite'];
export async function middleware(request: NextRequest) {
  let supabaseResponse = NextResponse.next({ request });
  const supabase = createServerClient(
    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL ?? '',
    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY ?? '',
    {
      cookies: {
        getAll() {
          return request.cookies.getAll();
        },
        setAll(cookiesToSet: Array<{ name: string; value: string; options?: CookieOptions }>) {
          cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value }) =>
            request.cookies.set(name, value),
          );
          supabaseResponse = NextResponse.next({ request });
          cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value, options }) =>
            supabaseResponse.cookies.set(name, value, options as Parameters<typeof supabaseResponse.cookies.set>[2]),
          );
        },
      },
    },
  );
  // getUser() validates the token with Supabase and auto-refreshes when expired.
  // This is Supabase's recommended pattern for Next.js middleware.
  const { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser();
  const pathname = request.nextUrl.pathname;
  if (OPEN_PATHS.some((p) => pathname.startsWith(p))) return supabaseResponse;
  const isPublic = PUBLIC_PATHS.some((p) => pathname.startsWith(p));
  if (!user && !isPublic) {
    const url = request.nextUrl.clone();
    url.pathname = '/login';
    return NextResponse.redirect(url);
  }
  if (user && isPublic) {
    const url = request.nextUrl.clone();
    url.pathname = '/';
    return NextResponse.redirect(url);
  }
  return supabaseResponse;
}
export const config = {
  matcher: ['/((?!_next|.*\\..*).*)'],
};

bash
command:

section='''### 6.9 Routing, redirects and "not found"

**Rule: no page a user can reach is deleted without a redirect, and no parent path is left without a page.** Next.js (App Router) only serves a URL if a `page.tsx` exists for that exact segment. `/contacts/[id]` existing does **not** make `/contacts` work. The same applies to `/voice` vs `/voice/[id]`.

#### Route map (final)

| URL | Status in the plan | Serves |
|---|---|---|
| `/` | **kept** | Home (Today + KPIs) |
| `/inbox` | **kept** | Inbox. Query: `view`, `lead`, `conversationId` (legacy, kept forever: the API puts it in notifications), `contactId` (legacy, resolved to the lead; fixes B1), `call` |
| `/contacts` | **kept** (not deleted) | Contacts list, `?view=table\\|pipeline&funnel=&stage=&search=` |
| `/contacts/[id]` | **kept** | Lead workspace (thread + LeadPanel). Only its `_components/*Card.tsx` are replaced. |
| `/schedule` | **kept** | Schedule, `?calendar=&view=&date=&appointment=` |
| `/payments` | **new** | Transactions + Needs attention (👤), `?tab=transactions\\|attention` |
| `/config/agents`, `/config/channels`, `/config/webhooks` | **kept, admin-only** | unchanged URL; moved into a guarded route group (below) |
| `/config/payments` | **kept, admin-only** | Payments setup (Stripe + Services & prices) |
| `/config/sequences`, `/config/communications`, `/templates` | **kept** | URLs unchanged. Only the nav groups them (Automation / Messaging). |
| `/admin`, `/admin/team`, `/admin/billing`, `/admin/api-keys`, `/admin/demo` | **kept** | URLs unchanged. API keys appears under Connections in the nav. |
| `/platform/demo-accounts` | **kept** | unchanged |

To limit churn, **only 4 URLs change**. Everything else is a nav regrouping.

#### Redirects (in `next.config.ts` → `redirects()`, server-side, query string preserved)

| From | To | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `/voice` | `/inbox?view=calls` | |
| `/voice/:id` | `/inbox?view=calls&call=:id` | opens the call drawer |
| `/config/funnel` | `/contacts?view=pipeline` | |
| `/integrations` | `/config/channels` | the mock page is removed |

Use `permanent: false` (307) during rollout, and switch to `true` (308) once it's stable, so nothing gets cached while routes are still moving.

#### Parent paths without a page (today they show a bare 404)

| URL | Today | After |
|---|---|---|
| `/config` | 404 | `config/page.tsx` redirects to the first Settings page the role can see (admin → `/config/agents`, agent → `/config/sequences`) |
| `/platform` | 404 | `platform/page.tsx` → `redirect('/platform/demo-accounts')` |
| `/voice` | page | redirect (above) |

#### 404 inside the app shell
There's no `not-found.tsx` or `error.tsx` anywhere today, so any wrong URL shows Next's default page, outside the sidebar and header.
- Add `app/(dashboard)/not-found.tsx`, shown **inside the shell**: "This page doesn't exist" + buttons **Inbox**, **Contacts** + a "Press ⌘K to search" hint.
- Add `app/(dashboard)/[...slug]/page.tsx`, which only calls `notFound()`. In the App Router, unmatched URLs otherwise go to the root `not-found`, which renders without the dashboard layout. Static and dynamic routes always win over this catch-all, so nothing real gets shadowed.
- Add `app/not-found.tsx` (root fallback, e.g. logged-out visitors) and `app/(dashboard)/error.tsx` (runtime errors with "Try again").

#### Entity not found (valid route, missing record)
| Case | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `/contacts/<deleted or invalid id>` | In-page "This contact no longer exists" + back to Contacts (today's behavior, restyled with the shared empty state) |
| `?lead=` / `?call=` / `?appointment=` / `?payment=` with a bad id | The drawer shows "Not found" and removes the param from the URL. The page underneath keeps working. |
| `/inbox?conversationId=<id of another org or deleted>` | The thread empty state shows "Conversation not available" (today it just stays blank) |

#### Role-protected routes
- Move the admin-only settings into a route group with a guard layout. **The URLs don't change**, because route groups aren't part of the URL:
  `app/(dashboard)/config/(admin)/{agents,channels,webhooks,payments}/page.tsx` + `config/(admin)/layout.tsx` (same pattern as `admin/layout.tsx`).
- Agent opens an admin-only URL → redirect with a toast "Only admins can open this page":
  - `/config/payments` → **`/payments`** (agents still have the operational view there);
  - the others → `/`.
- The API stays the real barrier (WS5). The page guard is for UX only.

#### Links generated by the API (must keep working)
| Source | Link today | Action |
|---|---|---|
| new message / call notifications | `/inbox?conversationId=<id>` | keep supported forever |
| contact created notification | `/contacts/<id>` | works (kept route) |
| appointment / follow-up notifications | `/schedule` | optional: add `?appointment=<id>` 🟡 |
| payment attention notifications (`appointment-events.publisher.ts:158`, `payments.service.ts:542`) | `/config/payments` | 🟡 change to `/payments?tab=attention`. Otherwise agents would land on an admin-only page. The redirect above covers old notifications. |
| password reset email | `/reset-password?token=` | see B10 |

#### Tests
- A route table test (Playwright, following the existing `visual/` setup): each old URL → expected final URL; `/config` and `/platform` redirect; an unknown URL renders the in-shell 404; an agent on `/config/channels` → `/`; an agent on `/config/payments` → `/payments`.
- A unit test that `next.config.ts` `redirects()` contains the 4 mappings.

You're right that this can happen in Next.js. A /contacts/[id] page does not make /contacts work; each URL needs its own page, so removing a parent page while keeping the child gives a 404 on the parent. The plan now has a rule: nothing is removed without a redirect, and no parent path is left without a page.

Old URL    Goes to
