import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import type { Page } from '@playwright/test';
/** A template color and the highest opacity the template uses it at. */
export type PaletteColor = [r: number, g: number, b: number, maxAlpha: number];
/**
 * The "original template": every color the design system defines in
 * globals.css (theme tokens and the literals used by its utilities), plus
 * black for the Radix dialog overlay (bg-black/75). Opaque tokens can be used
 * at any opacity (Tailwind `/10` modifiers); translucent literals such as the
 * white border tints only up to the opacity the template gives them.
 */
export function loadTemplatePalette(): PaletteColor[] {
  const css = readFileSync(path.join(__dirname, '../../src/app/globals.css'), 'utf8');
  const palette = new Map<string, PaletteColor>();
  const add = (r: number, g: number, b: number, alpha: number) => {
    const key = `${r},${g},${b}`;
    palette.set(key, [r, g, b, Math.max(alpha, palette.get(key)?.[3] ?? 0)]);
  };
  for (const [, hex] of css.matchAll(/#([0-9a-f]{6}|[0-9a-f]{3})\b/gi)) {
    const full = hex.length === 3 ? hex.split('').map((c) => c + c).join('') : hex;
    const [r, g, b] = [0, 2, 4].map((i) => parseInt(full.slice(i, i + 2), 16));
    add(r, g, b, 1);
  }
  for (const [, r, g, b, a] of css.matchAll(/rgba?\(\s*(\d+)[\s,]+(\d+)[\s,]+(\d+)(?:\s*[/,]\s*([\d.]+%?))?\s*\)/g)) {
    const alpha = a === undefined ? 1 : a.endsWith('%') ? parseFloat(a) / 100 : parseFloat(a);
    add(Number(r), Number(g), Number(b), alpha);
  }
  add(0, 0, 0, 0.75);
  return [...palette.values()];
}

  unlabeledControls: string[];
  foreignFonts: string[];
  spanishText: string[];
  horizontalOverflow: string[];
}

The Row, Group, Card and PanelSection matches are component props, not HTML attributes. The sidebar's "Sign out" title predates my work and sits outside the audited area. For the real ones I'll add a small Hint component on top of the app's existing Radix Tooltip. A disabled button doesn't fire pointer events, so Hint can wrap the trigger in a span, which keeps explanations like "Take over to send a link yourself" working.

bash
command:
cd /workspace/apps/web/src && cat components/ui/tooltip.tsx | head -31 && cat > components/ui/hint.tsx <<'EOF'
'use client';

import { Tooltip, TooltipContent, TooltipProvider, TooltipTrigger } from './tooltip';

interface HintProps {
  label: React.ReactNode;
  children: React.ReactElement;
  side?: 'top' | 'bottom' | 'left' | 'right';
  /**
   * Disabled buttons don't fire pointer events, so their tooltip never
   * opens. `wrap` puts the trigger on a span around the child instead —
   * use it to explain why an action is unavailable.
   */
  wrap?: boolean;
}

/** The design system's tooltip (native `title` attributes are not used). */
export function Hint({ label, children, side = 'top', wrap = false }: HintProps) {
  return (
    <TooltipProvider delayDuration={300}>
      <Tooltip>
        <TooltipTrigger asChild>{wrap ? <span className="inline-flex min-w-0 flex-1 basis-[calc(50%-4px)]">{children}</span> : children}</TooltipTrigger>
        <TooltipContent side={side} className="max-w-64 text-xs">
          {label}
        </TooltipContent>
      </Tooltip>
    </TooltipProvider>
  );
}
EOF

I'll seed a real database with three paid payments on an AI-handled conversation: one created by the AI, one legacy row with no origin, and one created by a person. Only the first two should count as AI-assisted.

bash
command:
cd /workspace/apps/api && cat > src/modules/analytics/ai-assisted-revenue.integration.spec.ts <<'EOF'
/**
 * "AI-assisted revenue" against a real PostgreSQL (packages/database/schemas):
 *   TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://... pnpm --filter @crm/api test ai-assisted-revenue
 * Skipped when TEST_DATABASE_URL is not set.
 */
import 'reflect-metadata';
import { randomUUID } from 'crypto';
import { DataSource } from 'typeorm';
import { AnalyticsService } from './analytics.service';
import { AnalyticsEventEntity } from './analytics-event.entity';

const url = process.env.TEST_DATABASE_URL;
const describeDb = url ? describe : describe.skip;

jest.setTimeout(60_000);

describeDb('AI-assisted revenue (PostgreSQL)', () => {
  let ds: DataSource;
  let analytics: AnalyticsService;

  beforeAll(async () => {
    ds = new DataSource({ type: 'postgres', url, entities: [`${__dirname}/../../**/*.entity.ts`] });
    await ds.initialize();
    analytics = new AnalyticsService(ds.getRepository(AnalyticsEventEntity), ds);
  });

  afterAll(async () => {
    await ds?.destroy();
  });

  it('counts links the AI (or an old row) created, never the ones a person created', async () => {
    const org = randomUUID();
    const contact = randomUUID();
    const conversation = randomUUID();
    const service = randomUUID();
    await ds.query(`INSERT INTO core.organizations (id, name, slug) VALUES ($1, 'Clinic', $2)`, [org, `clinic-${org}`]);
    await ds.query(`INSERT INTO clients.contacts (id, organization_id, first_name) VALUES ($1, $2, 'Ana')`, [contact, org]);
    // The AI handles this conversation right now.
    await ds.query(
      `INSERT INTO conversations.conversations (id, organization_id, contact_id, channel, bot_active) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, 'whatsapp', true)`,
      [conversation, org, contact],
    );

  async update(id: string, organizationId: string, dto: UpdateContactDto): Promise<ContactEntity> {
    const contact = await this.findById(id, organizationId);
    // Track changes to core identity fields
    const trackedFields = ['first_name', 'last_name', 'email', 'phone'] as const;
    const changedFields: Record<string, { from: unknown; to: unknown }> = {};
    for (const field of trackedFields) {
      const newVal = dto[field];
      if (newVal !== undefined && newVal !== contact[field]) {
        changedFields[field] = { from: contact[field] ?? null, to: newVal };
      }
    }
    // Capture originals BEFORE Object.assign (which would replace them) so the
    // merges below actually merge with the prior values, not with themselves.
    const prevInsights = (contact.ai_insights as Record<string, unknown>) ?? {};
    const prevCustomFields = (contact.custom_fields as Record<string, unknown>) ?? {};
    // Stage changes only go through updateStage/moveStageIfUnchanged (validated + recorded in
    // the funnel history). Callers such as AI tools pass raw input that may still carry it.
    const { lead_stage: _ignoredStage, ...changes } = dto as UpdateContactDto & { lead_stage?: unknown };
    Object.assign(contact, changes);
    // Shallow-merge, not replace: an update may report only `sentiment` (or a
    // single captured field) and must not wipe a still-valid `intent`/`summary`
    // or other custom fields captured earlier (incl. human-entered ones).
    if (dto.ai_insights !== undefined) {
      contact.ai_insights = { ...prevInsights, ...dto.ai_insights };
    }
    if (dto.custom_fields !== undefined) {
      contact.custom_fields = { ...prevCustomFields, ...dto.custom_fields };
      this.applyLeadScoreSignals(contact);
    }
    const saved = await this.contactRepo.save(contact);
    if (Object.keys(changedFields).length > 0) {
      void this.dataUpdateRepo.save(
        this.dataUpdateRepo.create({
          contact_id: id,
          organization_id: organizationId,
          changed_fields: changedFields,
          changed_by: null,
        }),
      );
    }
    this.rmqClient?.emit(RABBITMQ_QUEUES.CONTACT_UPDATED, {
      organization_id: organizationId,
      contact_id: id,
      changed_fields: Object.keys(changedFields),
      first_name: saved.first_name,
      last_name: saved.last_name,
    });
    // Captured/custom fields changed → the funnel re-checks BANT qualification.
    if (dto.custom_fields !== undefined) {
      this.rmqClient?.emit(RABBITMQ_QUEUES.CONTACT_DATA_CAPTURED, {
        organization_id: organizationId,
        contact_id: id,
      });
    }
    void this.webhookDispatcher?.dispatch('contact.updated', organizationId, { contact_id: id });
    return saved;
  }
  /**
   * Past appointments are deleted with the contact; upcoming bookings block
   * the deletion (cancel them first so the contact is told). Payments are kept
   * with a name/email snapshot.
   */
  async moveStageIfUnchanged(
    id: string,
    organizationId: string,
    expectedStageId: string,
    stageId: string,
    reason: string,
  ): Promise<boolean> {
    const result = await this.contactRepo
      .createQueryBuilder()
      .update(ContactEntity)
      .set({ lead_stage: stageId })
      .where('id = :id', { id })
      .andWhere('organization_id = :organizationId', { organizationId })
      .andWhere('lead_stage = :expectedStageId', { expectedStageId })
      .execute();
    if (!result.affected) return false;
    const contact = await this.findById(id, organizationId);
    this.recordStageChange(contact, organizationId, expectedStageId, stageId, null, 'automation', reason);
    return true;
  }
  private recordStageChange(
    contact: ContactEntity,
    organizationId: string,
    fromStageId: string | null,
    toStageId: string,
    changedBy: string | null,
    source: 'manual' | 'automation',
    reason: string | null,
  ): void {
    // Fire-and-forget history log
    void this.historyRepo.save(
      this.historyRepo.create({
        contact_id: contact.id,
        from_stage_id: fromStageId,
        to_stage_id: toStageId,
        changed_by: changedBy,
        source,
        reason,
      }),
    );
    this.rmqClient?.emit(RABBITMQ_QUEUES.CONTACT_STAGE_CHANGED, {
      organization_id: organizationId,
      contact_id: contact.id,
      first_name: contact.first_name,
      last_name: contact.last_name,
      from_stage_id: fromStageId,
      to_stage_id: toStageId,
    });
    void this.webhookDispatcher?.dispatch('funnel.stage.changed', organizationId, {
      contact_id: contact.id,
      from_stage_id: fromStageId,
      to_stage_id: toStageId,
    });
  }

function setup() {

  const org = channels.find((c) => (c as FakeChannel).name === 'org:org-1') as FakeChannel;
  const change = (table: string, event: 'INSERT' | 'UPDATE', row: Record<string, unknown>) =>
    act(() => {
      org.listeners
        .filter((l) => l.type === 'postgres_changes')
        .forEach((l) => {
          // Each listener was registered for one table/event; call the ones that match.
          const registered = (l as unknown as { filterSpec?: { table: string; event: string } }).filterSpec;
          if (!registered || (registered.table === table && registered.event === event)) l.callback({ new: row });
        });
    });
  return { queryClient, invalidate, org, change };
}
beforeEach(() => {

  vi.spyOn(FakeChannel.prototype, 'on').mockImplementation(function (this: FakeChannel, type, filter, callback) {
    original.call(this, type, filter, callback);
    if (type === 'postgres_changes') {
      const spec = filter as { table: string; event: string };
      (this.listeners[this.listeners.length - 1] as unknown as { filterSpec: unknown }).filterSpec = { table: spec.table, event: spec.event };
    }
    return this;
  });
});

  createdAt?: Date;

export function useNotifications() {
  const [notifications, setNotifications] = useState<Notification[]>(notificationStore);
  useEffect(() => {
    const fn = (n: Notification[]) => setNotifications(n);
    listeners.push(fn);
    return () => {
      listeners = listeners.filter((l) => l !== fn);
    };
  }, []);
  const add = useCallback((n: AddNotificationInput) => {
    if (n.id && notificationStore.some((x) => x.id === n.id)) return;
    const item: Notification = {
      ...n,
      id: n.id ?? Math.random().toString(36).slice(2),
      read: false,
      createdAt: n.createdAt ?? new Date(),
    };
    notificationStore = [item, ...notificationStore].slice(0, MAX_NOTIFICATIONS);
    broadcast();
  }, []);
  const markRead = useCallback((id: string) => {
    notificationStore = notificationStore.map((n) =>
      n.id === id ? { ...n, read: true } : n,
    );
    broadcast();
  }, []);
  const markAllRead = useCallback(() => {
    notificationStore = notificationStore.map((n) => ({ ...n, read: true }));
    broadcast();
  }, []);
  const unreadCount = notifications.filter((n) => !n.read).length;
  return { notifications, add, markRead, markAllRead, unreadCount };
}

bash
command:
cd /workspace && cat > scripts/supabase-realtime-audit.sql <<'EOF'
-- Supabase Realtime audit — READ ONLY. Run in the Supabase SQL editor and keep
-- the output with the plan (.claude/plans/inbox-handoff-realtime-security-plan.md, WS4.0).
--
-- Why: the browser subscribes to postgres_changes with the public anon key and
-- a client-chosen filter (organization_id=eq.<org>). That filter is NOT a
-- security boundary: only Row Level Security on the published tables is.
-- Broadcast topics (org:<id>, conversation:<id>) are public unless private
-- channels + realtime.messages policies are configured.

-- 1. Tables published to Realtime.
--    Expected by the web app: conversations.messages, conversations.conversations, voice.calls.
SELECT schemaname, tablename
  FROM pg_publication_tables
 WHERE pubname = 'supabase_realtime'
 ORDER BY 1, 2;

-- 2. RLS state of the published (and candidate) tables.
--    rls_on must be true for every published table.
SELECT n.nspname AS schema, c.relname AS "table",
       c.relrowsecurity AS rls_on, c.relforcerowsecurity AS rls_forced,
       c.relreplident AS replica_identity
  FROM pg_class c
  JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace
 WHERE (n.nspname, c.relname) IN (
         ('conversations', 'messages'),
         ('conversations', 'conversations'),
         ('voice', 'calls'),
         ('clients', 'contacts'))
 ORDER BY 1, 2;

-- 3. Policies on those schemas. Each published table needs a SELECT policy for
--    `authenticated` that restricts rows to the caller's organization
--    (e.g. organization_id = (SELECT organization_id FROM core.users WHERE auth_user_id = auth.uid()::text)).
SELECT schemaname, tablename, policyname, roles, cmd, qual
  FROM pg_policies
 WHERE schemaname IN ('conversations', 'voice', 'clients')
 ORDER BY 1, 2, 3;

-- 4. Broadcast / presence authorization (private channels).
--    Empty = every topic is public to anyone holding the anon key.
SELECT policyname, roles, cmd, qual, with_check
  FROM pg_policies
 WHERE schemaname = 'realtime'
 ORDER BY 1;

-- Also record from the dashboard: Realtime → Settings → "Allow public access"
-- (channel restrictions), and whether the conversations/voice schemas are exposed.
--
-- Decision gate: if any published table has rls_on = false, or its policies do
-- not restrict rows to the user's organization, securing Realtime (WS4.3:
-- RLS policies + private channels) becomes priority 1.
EOF

import { mockApi } from '@/test/msw/api';

import { TodayQueue } from './today-queue';

const team = vi.hoisted(() => ({ role: 'agent' }));
vi.mock('@/hooks/useTeam', () => ({ useCurrentUser: () => ({ data: { role: team.role }, isPending: false, isError: false }) }));
vi.mock('@/hooks/useToast', () => ({ toast: vi.fn() }));

const page = (items: unknown[]) => ({ items, meta: { total: items.length, page: 1, limit: 4, total_pages: 1 } });

beforeEach(() => {
  team.role = 'agent';
  mockApi('get', '/conversations/leads', {
    data: page([
      {
        contact: { id: 'c2', first_name: 'Luis', last_name: 'Gomez', lead_score: 30, tags: [] },
        channels: ['whatsapp'],
        bot_active: false,
        unread_count: 0,
        last_message: { content: 'I would rather talk to a person', created_at: '2026-03-15T10:00:00Z', direction: 'inbound', channel: 'whatsapp', conversation_id: 'conv-2' },
      },
    ]),
  });
  mockApi('get', '/automation/follow-ups', {
    data: { items: [{ id: 'step-1', contact_id: 'c2', title: 'Call Luis', action: 'call', due_at: '2026-03-15T09:00:00Z', contact: { first_name: 'Luis', last_name: 'Gomez' } }], total: 1 },
  });
  mockApi('get', '/appointments', { data: { items: [], meta: { total: 0, limit: 4, offset: 0 } } });
  mockApi('get', '/payments/attention', { data: [] });
});

function renderQueue() {
  const { wrapper } = createQueryWrapper();
  render(<TodayQueue />, { wrapper });
  return userEvent.setup();
}

describe('Today queue', () => {
  it('puts what waits for a person in one place, each linking to where it is worked', async () => {
    renderQueue();
    const needsHuman = await screen.findByRole('region', { name: 'Needs human' });
    expect(await within(needsHuman).findByRole('link', { name: /Luis Gomez/ })).toHaveAttribute('href', '/inbox?view=needs_human&lead=c2');
    const yourTurn = screen.getByRole('region', { name: 'Your turn' });
    expect(await within(yourTurn).findByText(/Call Luis/)).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByRole('region', { name: 'Needs outcome' })).toHaveTextContent('Every past appointment has an outcome.');
    // Agents resolve payment attention too.
    expect(screen.getByRole('region', { name: 'Payments attention' })).toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it('marks a follow-up done right from the queue', async () => {
    const done = mockApi('post', '/automation/follow-ups/step-1/complete', { data: { id: 'step-1', status: 'completed' } });
    const user = renderQueue();
    const yourTurn = await screen.findByRole('region', { name: 'Your turn' });
    await user.click(await within(yourTurn).findByRole('button', { name: 'Done' }));
    await waitFor(() => expect(done).toHaveLength(1));
  });

  it('hides payment attention from viewers', async () => {
    team.role = 'viewer';
    renderQueue();
    await screen.findByRole('region', { name: 'Needs human' });
    expect(screen.queryByRole('region', { name: 'Payments attention' })).not.toBeInTheDocument();
  });
});

---

## 13. Implementation status

Nothing is committed: review the working tree (`git status`). `git mv`/`git rm` moves are staged, so files show as renames; everything else is unstaged.

### Done

| Phase | Delivered |
|---|---|
| **P0 Security** | `@AdminOnly()` on every write of AI agent, automation agents/tools, channels (+ WhatsApp pairing QR), webhooks, payment services. Agents can see/resolve payment attention. Secrets masked: channel `page_access_token`/`app_secret`/`verify_token` (pattern-based), automation agents' `auth_header_value` → `has_auth_header`, and no longer echoed by `POST /channels`. Notification links → `/payments?tab=attention`, `/inbox?lead=`. API docs: calendar writes are user-only (D6). Web: `usePermissions`, `RoleGate`, role-filtered sidebar and ⌘K, `config/(admin)` route group (URLs unchanged), agents on payment setup → `/payments`. |
| **P1 Foundations & routing** | Redirects `/contacts`, `/contacts/:id`, `/config/funnel`, `/voice`, `/voice/:id`, `/integrations`. In-shell 404, error page, `/config` and `/platform` index redirects. Password reset reachable when signed out (B10). Mock `/integrations` removed. Dead components and hooks deleted; one stage hook; shared `lead-format`. |
| **P2 Handoff & reliable Inbox** | WS1: AI trigger skipped while a person controls the lead (all 3 producers, checked when the job runs). Replies from the wrong side → 409 (`AI_HAS_CONTROL` / `HUMAN_HAS_CONTROL`). `sender_type`/`sender_id`/`channel` stored on every reply. Lead-level explicit handoff (`POST /contacts/:id/handoff`) + legacy toggle applies to the whole lead. New channels inherit human control (D2). Due follow-ups become "Your turn" (D1). "Needs a person" notification. WS2: undeliverable messages → `failed` + reason. Composer with 5 states, picker removed, optimistic send. WS3: live-call banner (Retell), calls loaded on start, stale guard, no fake live transcript. WS4.2: key fix, ref-counted shared channels, presence lifecycle fix, reconnect resync, lead-scoped refresh, `contact.updated` push. |
| **P3 Lead panel** | `LeadPanel` (identity, decisions, actions, next, qualification, AI summary, related, details/tags/opt-outs) in the Inbox. Human payment links (only while a person has control), origin recorded, AI-assisted revenue excludes human links (D3). Payment events in the thread. `GET /conversations/leads` (one row per lead) with views and search. Conversation search fixed (B2). |
| **P4 Centralize in the Inbox** | Views: All open, Needs human, Your turn, Unread, Hot, AI active, Resolved, Calls, All contacts, Pipeline. Calls view + call drawer. Pipeline board/list inside the Inbox. `LeadChip` + peek drawer (`?lead=`) on other pages. Schedule deep link `?appointment=` + chips. Contacts/Voice/Funnel pages and the old contact cards, quick view and sidebar removed. |
| **P5 Home** | Today queue on the dashboard (Needs human, Your turn, Needs outcome, Payments attention). `/payments` operational page. |
| **P6 Settings & ⌘K** | Settings grouped (AI Agent, Automation, Messaging, Payments setup, Connections), role-filtered. ⌘K: server lead search + actions + role-filtered pages. |
| **P7 Channels** | WS8: per-channel opt-out (`opt-out:<channel>` tags), enforced on sends, the AI trigger, follow-up channel resolution and outbound calls. The AI tool tags the conversation's channel. Manage opt-outs in the panel. WS7: reachable channels, start WhatsApp/SMS from the panel or composer (the starter owns the lead), WhatsApp dispatch falls back to the contact's phone. |

### Verified
- API: typecheck + **541 tests** with `TEST_DATABASE_URL` (a real Postgres built from `packages/database/schemas`): lead list SQL, views, search, lead-level control, inheritance, activity payment events, undeliverable messages, AI-assisted revenue filter. 478 run without a DB; the DB suites skip.
- Web: typecheck, lint, **551 tests**, production build.
- Visual (Playwright, production build, mocked API): **45/46**. The failing one (`communication templates`) fails identically on the untouched baseline commit (stale snapshot, not caused by this work). New `visual/inbox.spec.ts` covers the Inbox flows and runs the design audit on every screen. Regression/billing baselines changed only where the sidebar or the billing copy changed on purpose; `team-page-main` / `admin-panel-main` were generated from the original code and match.

### How to run what needed extra setup
- DB integration specs: `TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://… pnpm --filter @crm/api test` (apply `packages/database/schemas/*.sql` first; `031` needs `pg_cron` only for its last block).
- Visual: `CHROMIUM_PATH=/path/to/chromium pnpm --filter @crm/web test:visual`.

### Still open (needs people outside the code)
- **Supabase:** run `scripts/supabase-realtime-audit.sql`. Then RLS on published tables + private channels (WS4.3, part 2).
- **n8n / ProSales owner:**
  - 409s while a person has control.

Contacts now live only in the Inbox, and the whole master plan is implemented (phases P0–P7). Nothing is committed: there's no git identity here and I didn't want to invent one. The work is in the working tree for you to review.


Verification: API 541 tests pass against a local Postgres built from your schema files; web 551 tests pass; typecheck, lint and the production build are clean. In Playwright against the production build, 45 of 46 screens pass. The one failure ("communication templates") fails the same way on the untouched original code, so it's an old stale baseline, not something I broke.


One place for leads: the Inbox


/contacts, /contacts/:id, /config/funnel and /voice are gone as screens. Their URLs redirect into the Inbox, so old links and bookmarks still work.
The Inbox shows one row per lead across all channels. Views: All open · Needs human · Your turn · Unread · Hot · AI active · Resolved · Calls · All contacts · Pipeline.
Every view opens the same thread (all channels, calls, payments, stage changes) and the same lead panel on the right: owner, stage, score, Call / Book / Payment link / Follow-up, what's next, captured data, AI summary, related items, opt-outs.
On other pages, a contact name opens that same panel in a side drawer, with "Open in Inbox".
The Dashboard starts with a "Today" queue: Needs human, Your turn, Needs outcome, Payments attention.

Your decisions, as built


Human takeover: the AI is not sent any event while a person has control, and late AI replies are rejected. The textbox stays locked while the AI has control. Taking over or returning to the AI applies to the whole lead (D2). A follow-up that falls due during a takeover becomes a "Your turn" task (D1).
"Reply via" picker removed: replies go to the channel the lead last wrote on.
Live calls: the banner shows "Call in progress · handled by Retell AI" with a timer. Transcript and recording appear when the call ends.
Payment links: agents can create them only while they have control. They don't count as AI-assisted revenue (D3), and agents can resolve payment attention items.
Opt-out per channel (D4): enforced on every send path, the AI, follow-ups and calls.
Starting WhatsApp/SMS: possible from the phone the contact gave.
Admin only (D5): AI agent, channels, webhooks and service prices. I also fixed API responses that exposed Facebook/Instagram tokens and the AI workflow's API key to any logged-in user.

Fixed along the way


Password reset was unreachable when signed out.
Inbox search did nothing.
Outbound messages were saved without channel or sender.
Messages that could never be delivered stayed "pending" forever with no error.
A wrong URL showed a bare 404 outside the app.

Things to know before you review


pnpm refused to download its pinned version (signature check failed), so I installed with the pnpm already on the machine. I got a Chromium from npm to run and screenshot the app.
I updated screenshot baselines only where the sidebar or billing text changed on purpose. For the Team and Admin pages I generated the new baselines from your original code, and my version matches them exactly.
The API's lint script doesn't work: ESLint isn't installed or configured there. That was already the case.

Still needs other people


Supabase admin: run scripts/supabase-realtime-audit.sql (read-only). Whether the realtime tables are restricted per organization can't be checked from the code.
Whoever owns n8n / ProSales: AI replies now get rejected while a person has control; handoff applies to the whole lead; the AI's own past messages show as AI in its history; the opt-out tool is now per channel. I also need them to say whether they send the ai.response.streaming event.
WhatsApp started from a phone number: Mexican mobile numbers may not match their WhatsApp ID (the 52 vs 521 prefix). Worth checking the number with WAHA before the first message.
